title: Which business structure fits?
intro: Answer four short questions for plain-language guidance on the three most common structures.
disclaimer: General guidance, not legal advice. SCS confirms the right structure for your situation and handles the registration.

options.label: Charitable, religious, educational or social, not for profit

questions.text: How many owners will there be?
Do you want the business's debts kept separate from your personal assets?
Do you plan to bring in investors or shareholders?

businessname.title: Business name registration
businessname.description: The simplest structure: the business and its owner are legally the same, so the owner is personally responsible for the business's obligations. Often a starting point for sole traders and small partnerships.

company.title: Limited company
company.description: A separate legal entity owned by its shareholders and run by directors. Liability is generally limited, and the structure suits businesses that want to bring in investors, build credibility or grow.

trustees.title: Incorporated trustees
trustees.description: The structure used for not-for-profit bodies with charitable, religious, educational or social purposes. The body is registered and holds property through its trustees.
